passages.text: Hear, O Israel: Today you are about to cross the Jordan to go in and dispossess nations greater and stronger than you, with large cities fortified to the heavens.
passages.sermon:
Israel, listen.
Today you are about to cross the Jordan River.
You will enter the land.
You will take possession of nations.
These nations are greater than you.
These nations are stronger than you.
They have large cities.
Their cities have strong walls.
Their cities are fortified up to the sky.
passages.original: שְׁמַ֣ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אַתָּ֨ה עֹבֵ֤ר הַיּוֹם֙ אֶת־ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן לָבֹא֙ לָרֶ֣שֶׁת גּוֹיִ֔ם גְּדֹלִ֥ים וַעֲצֻמִ֖ים מִמֶּ֑ךָּ עָרִ֛ים גְּדֹלֹ֥ת וּבְצֻרֹ֖ת בַּשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

passages.text: The people are strong and tall, the descendants of the Anakim. You know about them, and you have heard it said, “Who can stand up to the sons of Anak?”
passages.sermon:
The people are strong.
The people are tall.
They are descendants of the Anakim.
You know about these people.
You have heard about them.
People say, “Who can stand against the sons of Anak?”
passages.original: עַֽם־ גָּד֥וֹל וָרָ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י עֲנָקִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתָּ֤ה יָדַ֙עְתָּ֙ וְאַתָּ֣ה שָׁמַ֔עְתָּ מִ֣י יִתְיַצֵּ֔ב לִפְנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י עֲנָֽק׃

passages.text: But understand that today the LORD your God goes across ahead of you as a consuming fire; He will destroy them and subdue them before you. And you will drive them out and annihilate them swiftly, as the LORD has promised you.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
Today, know this.
The LORD your God goes ahead of you.
He goes before you like a consuming fire.
He will destroy these nations before you.
He will subdue them before you.
You will drive them out.
You will wipe them out quickly.
The LORD promised this to you.
passages.original: וְיָדַעְתָּ֣ הַיּ֗וֹם כִּי֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֶ֜יךָ הֽוּא־ הָעֹבֵ֤ר לְפָנֶ֙יךָ֙ אֵ֣שׁ אֹֽכְלָ֔ה ה֧וּא יַשְׁמִידֵ֛ם וְה֥וּא יַכְנִיעֵ֖ם לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וְהֽוֹרַשְׁתָּ֤ם וְהַֽאַבַדְתָּם֙ מַהֵ֔ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: When the LORD your God has driven them out before you, do not say in your heart, “Because of my righteousness the LORD has brought me in to possess this land.” Rather, the LORD is driving out these nations before you because of their wickedness.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
The LORD will drive these nations out before you.
Do not say in your heart, “The LORD has brought me in to possess this land because of my righteousness.”
The LORD is not giving you this land because you are righteous.
The LORD is driving out these nations before you because of their wickedness.
passages.original: אַל־ תֹּאמַ֣ר בִּלְבָבְךָ֗ בַּהֲדֹ֣ף יְהוָה֩ אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ אֹתָ֥ם׀ מִלְּפָנֶיךָ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ בְּצִדְקָתִי֙ הֱבִיאַ֣נִי יְהוָ֔ה לָרֶ֖שֶׁת אֶת־ הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֑את וּבְרִשְׁעַת֙ הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָאֵ֔לֶּה יְהוָ֖ה מוֹרִישָׁ֥ם מִפָּנֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: It is not because of your righteousness or uprightness of heart that you are going in to possess their land, but it is because of their wickedness that the LORD your God is driving out these nations before you, to keep the promise He swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD your God.
God is giving you their land.
God is not giving you their land because you are righteous.
God is not giving you their land because your heart is upright.
God is driving out these nations because they are wicked.
God is keeping the promise He swore to your fathers.
God made this promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
passages.original: לֹ֣א בְצִדְקָתְךָ֗ וּבְיֹ֙שֶׁר֙ לְבָ֣בְךָ֔ אַתָּ֥ה בָ֖א לָרֶ֣שֶׁת אֶת־ אַרְצָ֑ם כִּ֞י בְּרִשְׁעַ֣ת׀ הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָאֵ֗לֶּה יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ מוֹרִישָׁ֣ם מִפָּנֶ֔יךָ וּלְמַ֜עַן הָקִ֣ים אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֗ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֤ע יְהוָה֙ לַאֲבֹתֶ֔יךָ לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹֽב׃

passages.text: Understand, then, that it is not because of your righteousness that the LORD your God is giving you this good land to possess, for you are a stiff-necked people.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
He is giving you this good land.
He is not giving it to you because of your righteousness.
You are not righteous.
You are a stiff-necked people.
You are stubborn.
You do not deserve this land because of your own goodness.
passages.original: וְיָדַעְתָּ֗ כִּ֠י לֹ֤א בְצִדְקָֽתְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱ֠לֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵ֨ן לְךָ֜ אֶת־ הָאָ֧רֶץ הַטּוֹבָ֛ה הַזֹּ֖את לְרִשְׁתָּ֑הּ כִּ֥י עַם־ קְשֵׁה־ עֹ֖רֶף אָֽתָּה׃

passages.text: Remember this, and never forget how you provoked the LORD your God in the wilderness. From the day you left the land of Egypt until you reached this place, you have been rebelling against the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Israel, you are God’s chosen people.
You left Egypt by God’s power.
Remember what you did in the wilderness.
Do not forget how you made the LORD your God angry.
From the day you left Egypt, you rebelled against the LORD.
You kept rebelling until you arrived here.
passages.original: זְכֹר֙ אַל־ תִּשְׁכַּ֔ח אֵ֧ת אֲשֶׁר־ הִקְצַ֛פְתָּ אֶת־ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר לְמִן־ הַיּ֞וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ יָצָ֣אתָ׀ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֗יִם עַד־ בֹּֽאֲכֶם֙ עַד־ הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה מַמְרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם עִם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: At Horeb you provoked the LORD, and He was angry enough to destroy you.
passages.sermon: At Horeb, you provoked the LORD.\r\nThe LORD became very angry with you.\r\nThe LORD wanted to destroy you.
passages.original: וּבְחֹרֵ֥ב הִקְצַפְתֶּ֖ם אֶת־ יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּתְאַנַּ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה בָּכֶ֖ם לְהַשְׁמִ֥יד אֶתְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: When I went up on the mountain to receive the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant that the LORD made with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.
passages.sermon:
I went up on the mountain.
I went to receive the tablets of stone.
These tablets were the tablets of the covenant.
The LORD made this covenant with you.
I stayed on the mountain for forty days and forty nights.
I did not eat any bread.
I did not drink any water.
passages.original: בַּעֲלֹתִ֣י הָהָ֗רָה לָקַ֜חַת לוּחֹ֤ת הָֽאֲבָנִים֙ לוּחֹ֣ת הַבְּרִ֔ית אֲשֶׁר־ כָּרַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה עִמָּכֶ֑ם וָאֵשֵׁ֣ב בָּהָ֗ר אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יוֹם֙ וְאַרְבָּעִ֣ים לַ֔יְלָה לֶ֚חֶם לֹ֣א אָכַ֔לְתִּי וּמַ֖יִם לֹ֥א שָׁתִֽיתִי׃

passages.text: Then the LORD gave me the two stone tablets, inscribed by the finger of God with the exact words that the LORD spoke to you out of the fire on the mountain on the day of the assembly.
passages.sermon:
The LORD gave me two stone tablets.
God wrote on these tablets with His own finger.
The words on the tablets were the same words the LORD spoke to you.
The LORD spoke these words to you from the fire.
This happened on the mountain.
This was on the day when you all gathered together.
passages.original: וַיִּתֵּ֨ן יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י אֶת־ שְׁנֵי֙ לוּחֹ֣ת הָֽאֲבָנִ֔ים כְּתֻבִ֖ים בְּאֶצְבַּ֣ע אֱלֹהִ֑ים וַעֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כְּֽכָל־ הַדְּבָרִ֡ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּר֩ יְהוָ֨ה עִמָּכֶ֥ם בָּהָ֛ר מִתּ֥וֹךְ הָאֵ֖שׁ בְּי֥וֹם הַקָּהָֽל׃

passages.text: And at the end of forty days and forty nights, the LORD gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.
passages.sermon:
Moses went up the mountain.
He stayed there for forty days and forty nights.
At the end of forty days and forty nights, the LORD acted.
The LORD gave Moses two stone tablets.
These tablets were called the tablets of the covenant.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י מִקֵּץ֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים י֔וֹם וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים לָ֑יְלָה נָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י אֶת־ שְׁנֵ֛י לֻחֹ֥ת הָאֲבָנִ֖ים לֻח֥וֹת הַבְּרִֽית׃

passages.text: And the LORD said to me, “Get up and go down from here at once, for your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have corrupted themselves. How quickly they have turned aside from the way that I commanded them! They have made for themselves a molten image.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
The LORD gave me a command.
He said, "Get up."
He said, "Go down from here at once."
The LORD identified the people.
He said, "These are your people."
He said, "You brought them out of Egypt."
The LORD described the people.
He said, "They have corrupted themselves."
The LORD explained their actions.
He said, "They turned aside quickly from the way I commanded them."
He said, "They made a molten image for themselves."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י ק֣וּם רֵ֤ד מַהֵר֙ מִזֶּ֔ה כִּ֚י שִׁחֵ֣ת עַמְּךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוֹצֵ֖אתָ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם סָ֣רוּ מַהֵ֗ר מִן־ הַדֶּ֙רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ם עָשׂ֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם מַסֵּכָֽה׃

passages.text: The LORD also said to me, “I have seen this people, and they are indeed a stiff-necked people.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to me.
The LORD is the God who brought Israel out of Egypt.
The LORD said, “I have seen this people.”
The LORD saw the people of Israel.
The LORD said, “They are a stiff-necked people.”
The people of Israel are stubborn.
They do not listen or obey easily.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֣י לֵאמֹ֑ר רָאִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה עַם־ קְשֵׁה־ עֹ֖רֶף הֽוּא׃

passages.text: Leave Me alone, so that I may destroy them and blot out their name from under heaven. Then I will make you into a nation mightier and greater than they are.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God said, “Leave Me alone.
I will destroy this people.
I will erase their name from under heaven.
I will make you, Moses, into a nation.
Your nation will be stronger and greater than theirs.”
passages.original: הֶ֤רֶף מִמֶּ֙נִּי֙ וְאַשְׁמִידֵ֔ם וְאֶמְחֶ֣ה אֶת־ שְׁמָ֔ם מִתַּ֖חַת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה֙ אֽוֹתְךָ֔ לְגוֹי־ עָצ֥וּם וָרָ֖ב מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: So I went back down the mountain while it was blazing with fire, with the two tablets of the covenant in my hands.
passages.sermon:
Moses was on the mountain.
The mountain was burning with fire.
I turned and went down from the mountain.
I held the two tablets of the covenant in my hands.
passages.original: וָאֵ֗פֶן וָֽאֵרֵד֙ מִן־ הָהָ֔ר וְהָהָ֖ר בֹּעֵ֣ר בָּאֵ֑שׁ וּשְׁנֵי֙ לֻחֹ֣ת הַבְּרִ֔ית עַ֖ל שְׁתֵּ֥י יָדָֽי׃

passages.text: And I saw how you had sinned against the LORD your God; you had made for yourselves a molten calf. You had turned aside quickly from the way that the LORD had commanded you.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the people of Israel.
Moses saw what the people had done.
The people had sinned against the LORD their God.
The people made a calf out of metal for themselves.
The people turned away from the path God commanded.
The people left God's way very quickly.
passages.original: וָאֵ֗רֶא וְהִנֵּ֤ה חֲטָאתֶם֙ לַיהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם עֲשִׂיתֶ֣ם לָכֶ֔ם עֵ֖גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה סַרְתֶּ֣ם מַהֵ֔ר מִן־ הַדֶּ֕רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר־ צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶתְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: So I took the two tablets and threw them out of my hands, shattering them before your eyes.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Moses held the two tablets of the covenant in his hands.
Moses took hold of the two tablets.
Moses threw the tablets from his hands.
Moses shattered the tablets.
You saw Moses break the tablets.
passages.original: וָאֶתְפֹּשׂ֙ בִּשְׁנֵ֣י הַלֻּחֹ֔ת וָֽאַשְׁלִכֵ֔ם מֵעַ֖ל שְׁתֵּ֣י יָדָ֑י וָאֲשַׁבְּרֵ֖ם לְעֵינֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then I fell down before the LORD for forty days and forty nights, as I had done the first time. I did not eat bread or drink water because of all the sin you had committed in doing what was evil in the sight of the LORD and provoking Him to anger.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Moses spoke to the people.
Moses said, “I fell down before the LORD.”
I did this for forty days and forty nights.
I did this just as I had done the first time.
I did not eat bread.
I did not drink water.
I did this because of all your sin.
You sinned by doing what was evil in the sight of the LORD.
You made the LORD angry.
passages.original: וָֽאֶתְנַפַּל֩ לִפְנֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה כָּרִאשֹׁנָ֗ה אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יוֹם֙ וְאַרְבָּעִ֣ים לַ֔יְלָה לֶ֚חֶם לֹ֣א אָכַ֔לְתִּי וּמַ֖יִם לֹ֣א שָׁתִ֑יתִי עַ֤ל כָּל־ חַטַּאתְכֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חֲטָאתֶ֔ם לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְהַכְעִיסֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For I was afraid of the anger and wrath that the LORD had directed against you, enough to destroy you. But the LORD listened to me this time as well.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the people of Israel.
The LORD was very angry with the people of Israel.
The LORD wanted to destroy them.
I, Moses, was afraid of the LORD’s anger and wrath.
I prayed to the LORD for the people.
The LORD listened to me again at that time.
passages.original: כִּ֣י יָגֹ֗רְתִּי מִפְּנֵ֤י הָאַף֙ וְהַ֣חֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר קָצַ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם לְהַשְׁמִ֣יד אֶתְכֶ֑ם וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י גַּ֖ם בַּפַּ֥עַם הַהִֽוא׃

passages.text: The LORD was angry enough with Aaron to destroy him, but at that time I also prayed for Aaron.
passages.sermon: The LORD became very angry with Aaron.\r\nThe LORD wanted to destroy Aaron.\r\nAt that time, I prayed for Aaron.
passages.original: וּֽבְאַהֲרֹ֗ן הִתְאַנַּ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה מְאֹ֖ד לְהַשְׁמִיד֑וֹ וָֽאֶתְפַּלֵּ֛ל גַּם־ בְּעַ֥ד אַהֲרֹ֖ן בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽוא

passages.text: And I took that sinful thing, the calf you had made, and burned it in the fire. Then I crushed it and ground it to powder as fine as dust, and I cast it into the stream that came down from the mountain.
passages.sermon:
You made a sinful calf.
I took the calf you made.
I burned the calf in the fire.
I crushed the calf.
I ground it until it became fine like dust.
I threw the dust into the stream.
The stream flowed down from the mountain.
passages.original: וְֽאֶת־ חַטַּאתְכֶ֞ם אֲשֶׁר־ עֲשִׂיתֶ֣ם אֶת־ הָעֵ֗גֶל לָקַחְתִּי֮ וָאֶשְׂרֹ֣ף אֹת֣וֹ׀ בָּאֵשׁ֒ וָאֶכֹּ֨ת אֹת֤וֹ טָחוֹן֙ הֵיטֵ֔ב עַ֥ד אֲשֶׁר־ דַּ֖ק לְעָפָ֑ר וָֽאַשְׁלִךְ֙ אֶת־ עֲפָר֔וֹ אֶל־ הַנַּ֖חַל הַיֹּרֵ֥ד מִן־ הָהָֽר׃

passages.text: You continued to provoke the LORD at Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth-hattaavah.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel made the LORD angry.
They did this at Taberah.
They did this at Massah.
They did this at Kibroth-hattaavah.
They kept provoking the LORD in these places.
passages.original: וּבְתַבְעֵרָה֙ וּבְמַסָּ֔ה וּבְקִבְרֹ֖ת הַֽתַּאֲוָ֑ה מַקְצִפִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם אֶת־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And when the LORD sent you out from Kadesh-barnea, He said, “Go up and possess the land that I have given you.” But you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God. You neither believed Him nor obeyed Him.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
He sent you out from Kadesh-barnea.
He spoke to you.
He said, “Go up and take the land I have given you.”
You did not obey His command.
You rebelled against Him.
You did not believe Him.
You did not listen to His voice.
passages.original: וּבִשְׁלֹ֨חַ יְהוָ֜ה אֶתְכֶ֗ם מִקָּדֵ֤שׁ בַּרְנֵ֙עַ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר עֲלוּ֙ וּרְשׁ֣וּ אֶת־ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לָכֶ֑ם וַתַּמְר֗וּ אֶת־ פִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֤א הֶֽאֱמַנְתֶּם֙ ל֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם בְּקֹלֽוֹ׃

passages.text: You have been rebelling against the LORD since the day I came to know you.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the Israelites.
The Israelites often rebelled against the LORD.
They started rebelling from the first day Moses knew them.
They continued to rebel against the LORD.
passages.original: מַמְרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם עִם־ יְהוָ֑ה מִיּ֖וֹם דַּעְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: So I fell down before the LORD for forty days and forty nights, because the LORD had said He would destroy you.
passages.sermon:
Moses is speaking to the Israelites.
The LORD had said He would destroy the Israelites.
I fell down before the LORD.
I did this for forty days.
I did this for forty nights.
I fell down because the LORD had said He would destroy you.
passages.original: וָֽאֶתְנַפַּ֞ל לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אֵ֣ת אַרְבָּעִ֥ים הַיּ֛וֹם וְאֶת־ אַרְבָּעִ֥ים הַלַּ֖יְלָה אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִתְנַפָּ֑לְתִּי כִּֽי־ אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה לְהַשְׁמִ֥יד אֶתְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: And I prayed to the LORD and said, “O Lord GOD, do not destroy Your people, Your inheritance, whom You redeemed through Your greatness and brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to God.
Moses prayed to the LORD.
Moses said, “O Lord GOD, do not destroy Your people.
These people belong to You.
They are Your inheritance.
You redeemed them by Your greatness.
You brought them out of Egypt.
You used Your mighty hand to save them.”
passages.original: וָאֶתְפַּלֵּ֣ל אֶל־ יְהוָה֮ וָאֹמַר֒ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אַל־ תַּשְׁחֵ֤ת עַמְּךָ֙ וְנַחֲלָ֣תְךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּדִ֖יתָ בְּגָדְלֶ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁר־ הוֹצֵ֥אתָ מִמִּצְרַ֖יִם בְּיָ֥ד חֲזָקָֽה׃

passages.text: Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Overlook the stubbornness of this people and the wickedness of their sin.
passages.sermon:
God, You have servants.
Their names are Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Remember them.
Do not look at the stubbornness of this people.
Do not look at their wickedness.
Do not look at their sin.
passages.original: זְכֹר֙ לַעֲבָדֶ֔יךָ לְאַבְרָהָ֥ם לְיִצְחָ֖ק וּֽלְיַעֲקֹ֑ב אַל־ תֵּ֗פֶן אֶל־ קְשִׁי֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְאֶל־ רִשְׁע֖וֹ וְאֶל־ חַטָּאתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Otherwise, those in the land from which You brought us out will say, ‘Because the LORD was not able to bring them into the land He had promised them, and because He hated them, He has brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.’
passages.sermon:
God brought the Israelites out of Egypt.
God promised to bring the Israelites into a new land.
If God destroys the Israelites in the wilderness, people in Egypt will speak.
They will say, “The LORD was not able to bring them into the land He promised them.”
They will also say, “The LORD hated them.”
They will say, “He brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.”
passages.original: פֶּן־ יֹאמְר֗וּ הָאָרֶץ֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הוֹצֵאתָ֣נוּ מִשָּׁם֒ מִבְּלִי֙ יְכֹ֣לֶת יְהוָ֔ה לַהֲבִיאָ֕ם אֶל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם וּמִשִּׂנְאָת֣וֹ אוֹתָ֔ם הוֹצִיאָ֖ם לַהֲמִתָ֥ם בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

passages.text: But they are Your people, Your inheritance, whom You brought out by Your great power and outstretched arm.”
passages.sermon:
God, these people belong to You.
They are Your people.
They are Your inheritance.
You brought them out of Egypt.
You used Your great power.
You saved them with Your mighty, outstretched arm.
passages.original: וְהֵ֥ם עַמְּךָ֖ וְנַחֲלָתֶ֑ךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הוֹצֵ֙אתָ֙ בְּכֹחֲךָ֣ הַגָּדֹ֔ל וּבִֽזְרֹעֲךָ֖ הַנְּטוּיָֽה׃פ
